strengths: Novel stepwise decomposition framework elegantly decomposes intractable trajectory-level optimization into tractable per-step posterior alignment, well-suited to discrete diffusion models
Sound theoretical contributions with Theorem 4.1 establishing equivalence between stepwise and trajectory objectives, and Propositions 4.2-4.3 guaranteeing correctness of the empirical loss

Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse domains (DNA, protein, language) with consistent improvements: 12.3% over DRAKES on DNA design, GSM8K 78.6→80.7, 30.9% relative improvement on AlpacaEval
Methodological generality: works with arbitrary reward functions (overcomes DPO's Bradley-Terry restriction) and reduces to DPO as special case
Thorough ablation studies examining β sensitivity, sample size N effects, and iterative labeling, with clear interpretable results
Clear presentation, strong baselines (CG, SMC, TDS, CFG, DRAKES), and detailed hyperparameters supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Theorem 4.1's additive factorization assumption r̂(x₀:T,c) = Σₜ w(t)r̂ₜ(xₜ,c) is restrictive with no analysis of performance under violation; lacks empirical validation that used reward models satisfy this property

Core empirical loss (Eq. 12-13) is a standard Monte Carlo approximation of KL divergence between Boltzmann policies; fundamental novelty is primarily in applying existing preference optimization machinery to stepwise decomposition
Language modeling improvements are modest (2.1 points on GSM8K) without error bars or statistical significance tests; only 2 epochs of UltraFeedback training suggests potential undertaining

Incomplete experimental comparisons: no direct comparison with other discrete diffusion alignment methods [58,69]; language model evaluated only against base model, not other preference optimization methods on same architecture

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity with dramatically different β values across tasks (0.92, 0.4, 0.064 for DNA; 0.047, 0.063 for protein) requiring task-specific tuning; limited guidance for practitioners

Missing implementation details: computational cost vs baselines not discussed (especially for iterative labeling); justification for always using pre-trained model as reference; reliance on iterative labeling for DNA/protein contradicts 'offline' framing
Minimal failure analysis: only brief limitation discussion; no empirical study of behavior with noisy/misspecified reward functions despite mentioning this limitation
